bounds.domain: One existing Maps window and organization, paired burst/sustained buckets, clock0..8 initially4, quarter-token units; two configurations exchange the limiting dimension. Only successful admissions persist refill state.
bounds.atomicity: A Maps admission and its receipt are one existing Durable Object SQLite transaction. The model starts after credential, policy and window admission.
bounds.progress: No temporal or fairness claim; a clock that never advances may prevent refill indefinitely.

limitations: No proof of JavaScript floating-point rounding or arbitrary numeric limits.
Credential ownership, subscription policy, allowance-window transitions, tombstone retention and cross-organization routing remain separate obligations.
The strict hook executes the real controller on Miniflare SQLite with a controlled fixture clock; this is scenario correspondence, not general TypeScript refinement.

The composed tile-route scenario uses Hono, the production route and Google provider adapter, a Miniflare native global limiter, and real Maps/rate-state SQLite Durable Objects. Account authentication and the primary locked policy are explicit fixtures; the provider transport returns controlled bytes. It does not boot all application middleware or establish live authorization, deployed rate-limit behavior, or Google availability. The 67-request scenario is implementation evidence beyond this model's finite bounds, not exhaustive refinement.
